The self-learning system has two opposite traps, and they look identical from a
distance — a loop's output metric reads flat (`scored: 0`, 0 champions, 0 routed
ideas):

1. **Genuinely dark** — a loop built, shipped, then left un-armed (or wedged), so
   it produces nothing. Rots silently; the ranker prioritizes on a dead signal.
2. **Armed but young** — a loop that *is* running correctly and simply has
   nothing to process yet.

Telling them apart is the whole game, and you can only do it by reading the
**live gate state** + **whether there is anything due to process** — never by
inferring from the flat metric alone.

## The triple gate

A frontier learning loop (the 10 dark loops in `LEARNING_SINGLETONS`,
`packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/seed-learning-singletons.ts`) runs **only
when all three are true**:

1. **Routine active** — a `@singleton/bp-singleton-<id>-0` cadence row that is
   `active = true` (the blueprint seeds it **inactive**).
2. **Flag ON** — e.g. `papercusp-calibration-markets`. **Note (2026-06-23):** all
   frontier loop flags were bulk-flipped to default ON in `FLAG_DEFAULTS` as part
   of plan `flip-dark-flags-default-on-2026-06-23` and removed from
   `KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS`. On a standard install this gate is now **auto-satisfied** —
   the primary live blockers are routine active (gate 1) and governor budget (gate 3).
   The flag gate still matters as a kill-switch (flip OFF to quiesce a loop without
   darkening the routine) and for loops on fresh installs before the P-001 arming
   campaign has run.
3. **Governor allows** — a `learning_governor_loops` row whose verdict is
   `allow`. **Subtle:** `budgetUsd = NULL` ⇒ `unbudgeted` ⇒ refuse, but for a
   `per-cycle` loop `budgetUsd = 0` (not null) **ALLOWS** — `checkLoopVerdict`
   (`learning-governor/core.ts:101`) short-circuits per-cycle to allow before any
   floor check. For a SQL-only sweep that never spends, `0` is a legitimate armed
   value ("0 is honest", `calibration/governor.ts`). So "the budget is 0" does
   **not** mean dark; "the budget is NULL" does.

**A flag being ON is NOT "armed"** (a NULL-budget or inactive-routine loop is
dark despite the flag) — and equally, **a flat metric is NOT "dark".**

## The 2026-06-14 calibration case (the inverse trap)

calibration *looked* dark: `calibration_summary` showed `scored: 0` with the open
`fix-survival` bets climbing 19 → 53 in a session — exactly the silhouette of a
sweep that places bets but never resolves them. The audit (wrongly) called it a
dark loop starving the ranker's weight-8 `calibration` feature, and the owner
ratified "arm it."

A **read-first DB check before arming** (`harness_admin@localhost:5432/papercusp`)
showed there was nothing to arm — all three gates were already open:

- routine `@singleton/bp-singleton-calibration-0`: `active=t`, firing on its 6 h
  cadence (no legacy `papercup/calibration-resolve` row → no collision — `papercup`
  was this install's harness slug at the time, pre the 2026-06-19/20 rename to
  `papercusp`; see the "Current behavior (2026-07-02)" note below);
- flag `papercusp-calibration-markets`: ON;
- governor `calibration-markets`: `enabled=t`, `per-cycle`, `budget_usd=0` →
  `checkLoopVerdict` **allows**.

The real cause of `scored: 0` was **young bets**, not a dead sweep:
`SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE horizon_ts <= now() AND outcome IS NULL)` returned
**0 overdue-unresolved** — all 58 open bets mature in the *future* (earliest
~14 days out; `fix-survival` has a ~14-day survival window). The sweep runs every
6 h and correctly resolves nothing until the first bets come due. The ranker's
feature contributes 0 because nothing has matured — it lights up on its own at
maturation. **Arming would have been pointless churn on a working loop.** (Full
write-up: `relight-self-learning-edges-2026-06-14` D-009.)

## How to tell dark from young

- **`improvements:learning_loops`** (the dark-loop health surface, P-030) — per
  loop: `firing` / `stale` (active but not firing — a wedge) / `dark-by-design`
  (frontier, unarmed) / `should-be-on-but-dark` (an always-on loop gone dark — a
  real gap) / `absent`, plus the `@singleton`↔legacy `collision`. Start here.
- **Read the gates, not the metric:** the routine `active` flag + `last_fired_at`,
  the feature flag, and the `learning_governor_loops` row (`budget_usd` NULL vs 0,
  `enabled`). A loop `firing` on cadence with all gates open is NOT dark.
- **Check for due-but-unresolved work, not just a flat output:** the dead-sweep
  signal is *overdue and unprocessed* (e.g. `horizon_ts <= now() AND outcome IS
  NULL` for calibration bets; an old `armed` tripwire window long past close; a
  stuck claim past its stale window) — not merely "0 results". A flat metric on a
  young system is expected.

## Arming a genuinely-dark loop (the per-lane runbook)

`@singleton` routine `active` **+** a governor verdict of `allow`
(`registerLearningLoop`; for a SQL-only loop `budget_usd` 0 already allows) **+**
flag ON (now default true for all frontier loops since 2026-06-23; verify it
hasn't been manually killed). Arm the **right** row —
`@singleton/bp-singleton-<id>-0`, never the legacy bespoke row (both
active is the D-023 double-state, reported by `improvements:learning_loops` as
`collision`). This is a **coordinated frontier campaign** (the
`self-learning-frontier` P-001 gate arms all parked lanes together); prefer it
over a hand-flip. And **always read the live row first** — that read is what kept
this exact session from "arming" an already-armed loop.

**Current behavior (2026-07-02):** the legacy row's `install_slug` used to be
hardcoded to the literal `'papercup'` in `seed-learning-singletons.ts`. That was
quietly broken by the papercup→papercusp rename (owner-directed, 2026-06-19/20,
completed across the primary stores) — post-rename, legacy bespoke routines live
under `install_slug='papercusp'`, so the hardcoded `'papercup'` lookup no longer
matched anything and the collision guard / `--retire-legacy` pass silently found
nothing to act on. `seed-learning-singletons.ts` now resolves the slug via
`operatorHomeHarnessSlug()` (`packages/operator-core/lib/harness/operator-home-harness.ts`)
instead — the single pointer for "which pot is the workspace's operator home,"
defaulting to `papercusp` and overridable via `PAPERCUSP_HIVE_HOME_SLUG`. So when
arming today, read the legacy row under the **current** home-harness slug
(`papercusp` on this install), not the literal string `papercup` — the 2026-06-14
case study above predates the rename and used the slug that was correct at the
time.

**Scout has an additional workspace-level gate (P-051, added 2026-06-14):**
`checkScoutWorkspaceCeiling` (`learning-governor/core.ts`) sums every
`scout:<pot>` registrant's ledgered spend in the workspace and refuses a NEW
cycle once the total crosses `DEFAULT_SCOUT_WORKSPACE_CEILING_USD` ($10).
This is NOT the triple-gate (scout seeds `singletonActive:true`, so it's
always-on, not a dark frontier loop), but it matters if scout cycles stop firing
unexpectedly: the workspace aggregate may be exhausted even when each per-pot
cap looks fine. Tune via `PAPERCUSP_SCOUT_WORKSPACE_CEILING_USD`.

## The general lesson

Two sibling failure shapes, one class:

- **Never-armed:** a loop seeded inactive behind a default-OFF flag (or NULL
  governor budget) that nobody finished arming. No error, just no output.
- **Wedged:** an *active* loop whose liveness mechanism is keyed on a timestamp
  nobody writes (claim with no `assigned_at`; autoloop stuck `status='running'`),
  so its stale-reclaim never fires. See
  [improvement-implement-lane-wedge-triad](/internal/docs/agent-insights/improvement-implement-lane-wedge-triad).

Both are invisible without a health surface — *and* both can be impersonated by a
healthy-but-young loop, so verify before you act. When you ship a learning loop,
answer "how will anyone know if it goes dark — and how will they tell dark from
young?" If you add a "skip while in-flight" guard, it needs both a **written**
liveness timestamp and a **tested** stale path (pinned by an ordering invariant,
e.g. worker-timeout < orphan-threshold < stale-claim-window).
